text:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up — I prototyped two service auth patterns and want feedback. TL;DR: project-scoped API keys vs org-level service principals + impersonation.

trevor: high level first — what problem are we prioritizing? simplicity for customers or least-privilege defaults?

maya: both, but leaning least-privilege. We see customers accidentally creating org-wide keys and blasting quotas. We should make the safe path the easy one. :warning:

sam: agree on least-privilege. Curious about developer ergonomics — creating a new key per env/team is noisy. How do we keep UX low-friction?

maya: two patterns: 1) API Key (opaque) tied to project: single header, simple rotation. 2) Service Principal (JWT) at org-level that can impersonate a project-scoped actor via short-lived STS tokens.

lisa: can you show a tiny example of how the impersonation flow would look?

maya: sure — rough sketch:
```
# org service principal (long-lived creds) calls STS
POST /sts/assume-role
{ "principal_id": "svc-redwood-analytics", "target_project": "proj-123", "ttl": 300 }

# response
{ "access_token": "eyJ...", "expires_in": 300, "actor": "proj-123:svc-analytics" }

# then call inference API with project-scoped actor
Authorization: Bearer eyJ...
```

trevor: so tokens are short lived and carry actor = project:service. Good for audit and scoping. How do we store keys so lookup is fast at runtime?

maya: store org principals in KVS by id, project keys in project shard. Lookup order: check bearer token actor claim; if absent, fall back to API-key table. We must make lookup O(1) with memcache for hot keys.

sam: what's the plan for migration? We have thousands of existing API keys in db: some are used across multiple projects.

maya: migration steps I propose:
- Introduce compatibility layer: accept old keys and map to a temporary actor (legacy:actor-id)
- Run telemetry to find cross-project usage
- Offer a one-click split tool in Console to create project-scoped keys and update bindings
- After 90 days, block cross-project tokens and require explicit impersonation via STS

lisa: what about RBAC roles? We need clear verbs for service principals — call, list-models, manage-rollouts, billing-read.

maya: agreed. Minimal role set for services: inference.invoke, model.catalog.read, metrics.write. Admin roles separate. Roles are attached to actor (project:svc-name) and enforced in our gateway.

trevor: enforcement options: API gateway middleware vs runtime-level check. Middleware is cheap but can be bypassed by internal service calls. Prefer runtime checks as canonical.

maya: yes — runtime should be canonical. Gateway does fast reject for malformed tokens and coarse rate limits. Runtime enforces role checks and quota accounting.

infra-bot: deploy check: svc-auth-refactor branch has red CI: failing integration tests for token rotation. See https://ci.redwood/7891

maya: noted, will look. Two open risks: audit log volume (STS churn will spike logs) and key rotation UX for customers.

sam: for audit, we can sample non-admin events and keep full logs for admin ops. But must keep immutable records for billing queries.

lisa: rotation UX: propose Console shows active short-lived tokens and a rotation policy config. Also provide SDK helpers to auto-refresh STS and fall back to cached project key.

trevor: performance impact? extra STS hop per startup might add ~50ms. We can cache STS tokens per instance for TTL. For serverless cold starts, allow embedding project key in environment (opt-in) but mark it high-risk.

maya: implementation milestones (rough):
- phase 1 (2w): STS prototype + memcache lookup + gateway validation
- phase 2 (3w): Console UI for split/migration + telemetry dashboards
- phase 3 (2w): rollouts, canary on a small set of customers, deprecation plan

sam: 👍 on plan. One more ask: document the attacker model in RFC (token theft, cross-project misuse, compromised CI).

maya: will update RFC with attacker model and tests. Any objections to defaulting to project-scoped keys and making org principals explicitly opt-in?

trevor: no objections. Strongly prefer explicit opt-in for org-wide principals.

lisa: same. :thumbsup:

maya: great — I'll push an RFC update and queue a design review. Thanks all.

infra-bot: maya added label `rfc-updated` to thread.
